title: Postgres goes down in the middle of a load
summary: Starts the pg_books load, stops the Postgres container for about 5 seconds while it runs, then starts it again and reports the final job status, whether the table has exactly the expected rows (none lost, none doubled) and the warnings. It may legitimately fail: the point is to show what really happens.

engine.label: openetl job run pg_books (Postgres stopped mid-run)

steps.title: Empty the books table
steps.explain: Starts clean before the reference run.

steps.title: Reference run without any fault
steps.explain: Establishes how many rows a healthy run writes, so the faulty run has a real number to meet.

steps.title: Count rows after the reference run
steps.explain: This is the expected row count.

steps.title: Empty the books table again
steps.explain: Clears the reference rows so the faulty run starts from nothing.

steps.title: Read sample rows of books (Before)
steps.explain: Shows the table before the faulty run: it was just dropped.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM books ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5

steps.title: Start the pipeline in the background
steps.explain: The job must be running while the database is taken away.

steps.title: Let the job run for 4 seconds
steps.explain: Gives the job time to get into its work before the fault.

steps.title: Stop the Postgres container
steps.explain: The fault: the database disappears in the middle of the run.

steps.title: Keep Postgres down for 5 seconds
steps.explain: Long enough for the job to hit connection errors.

steps.title: Start Postgres again and wait until healthy
steps.explain: The database comes back. The job may or may not recover.

steps.title: Wait for the job to finish
steps.explain: Collects the final status and warnings of the interrupted job.

steps.title: Make sure Postgres is running
steps.explain: Safety net: leaves the lab database running whatever happened above.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: What the job says happened after the outage.

steps.title: Job reported 0 warnings
steps.explain: Warnings show what the job noticed about the outage.

steps.title: No warning or error lines in the output
steps.explain: The actual warning and error text, if any.

steps.title: Count rows in books
steps.explain: The real number of rows in the table.

steps.title: Row count equals the reference run
steps.explain: Fewer rows means data was lost.

steps.title: Count duplicated chunks
steps.explain: Rows that repeat the same chunk would mean data was doubled.

args.sql: SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT (source_filename, sequence_index)) FROM books

steps.title: No chunk is stored twice
steps.explain: Retrying a write must not double rows.

steps.title: Read sample rows of books (After)
steps.explain: Shows the table after the outage and the retry.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM books ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5
